payload.instructions: Preserve all candidate IDs and distinctions. Broader parent themes organize evidence; they do not imply measurement equivalence.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.interpretation: common or complementary evidence
themes.name: theme

themes.disagreements: Brain metastases presence (052) is a strong prognostic factor without effect modification, whereas calvarium lesions (057) and location (051) show complementary signals for effect modification.
themes.interpretation: Features describing the presence, location, and radiographic characteristics of brain metastases, showing a mix of strong prognostic signals and evidence for treatment effect modification.
themes.name: CNS Metastasis and Intracranial Involvement

themes.disagreements: Brainstem signal (054) has more robust support across multiple effect-estimation methods than brainstem size (055).
themes.interpretation: Evaluation of brainstem signal and size, where the primary evidence emerges in effect modification rather than main treatment or outcome effects.
themes.name: Brainstem Morphological Assessment

themes.disagreements: Cancer diagnosis (058) has moderate treatment-prediction support, while cancer location (059) lacks consistent signal across all roles.
themes.interpretation: Broad cancer diagnosis and primary location, which primarily serve as indicators of treatment assignment or exhibit no significant modeling signal.
themes.name: General Cancer Characteristics

themes.disagreements: Fatigue (060) is a powerful prognostic factor and candidate effect modifier, whereas calorie intake (056) is primarily associated with treatment prediction.
themes.interpretation: Nutritional status and cancer-related fatigue, showing strong prognostic value and associations with treatment prediction.
themes.name: Patient Systemic and Symptomatic State

themes.disagreements: Signals are primarily concentrated in treatment prediction (predictive forest) and effect modification (r-learner, causal forest), with limited outcome main-effect evidence.
themes.interpretation: Molecular and tumor markers showing strong evidence of both confounding (treatment prediction) and effect modification.
themes.name: Molecular and Biomarker Indicators

themes.disagreements: Predictive forest suggests strong treatment prediction for several features, but univariable and penalized models show inconsistent or weak outcome signals.
themes.interpretation: Neuroimaging characteristics that predominantly predict treatment assignment, suggesting a confounding role.
themes.name: Neuroimaging Features

themes.disagreements: Carboplatin shows strong outcome signals but negligible treatment prediction; cefepime shows virtually no signal.
themes.interpretation: Clinical administration markers, where one acts as a strong prognostic factor and the other is non-informative.
themes.name: Clinical and Medication Factors

themes.disagreements: No significant signals across any modeling family.
themes.interpretation: Comorbidities with no empirical evidence for a causal or prognostic role.
themes.name: Other Comorbidities

themes.disagreements: Clinical phenotype is a strong treatment predictor, while decline and severity score primarily show as effect modifiers.
themes.interpretation: General markers of clinical status and severity, manifesting as both confounders and effect modifiers.
themes.name: Clinical Severity and Status

themes.disagreements: Cycle count shows moderate support across roles but lacks the strength of the specific regimen marker.
themes.interpretation: Treatment-related history and regimen specifics.
themes.name: Treatment Regimen and Dosage

themes.disagreements: Strong confounding evidence for surgical history and renal stage, contrasted by a strong effect modification signal for CK5/6 expression.
themes.interpretation: Biomarkers and patient history including organ-specific markers and pathological expression.
themes.name: Pathological and Systemic Markers

themes.disagreements: Predictive forest suggests outcome importance, but univariable signals are weak.
themes.interpretation: Neuro-imaging signal assessment.
themes.name: Cerebral Imaging

themes.disagreements: Cough presence (090) is a weak signal compared to the strong signals seen in COPD (087, 088). CAP presence (081) primarily predicts the outcome rather than the treatment.
themes.interpretation: Features related to chronic and acute respiratory conditions. COPD presence and severity show strong, consistent signals for both treatment prediction and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: COPD and Respiratory Health

themes.disagreements: Coronary artery disease (089) shows negligible signal compared to the aggregate comorbidity count (082).
themes.interpretation: Broad measures of patient sickness. Total comorbidity count is a highly significant predictor of both treatment assignment and outcome.
themes.name: General Health and Comorbidity Burden

themes.disagreements: CMP results (084) strongly predict treatment but not the outcome, whereas CBC (083) and contrast concentration (086) provide little to no evidence for any role.
themes.interpretation: Qualitative and quantitative results from standard blood and imaging panels.
themes.name: Laboratory Diagnostics

themes.disagreements: Unlike the respiratory/comorbidity features, confusion presents as a signal of treatment effect heterogeneity rather than a main-effect confounder.
themes.interpretation: Assessment of current neurological state upon presentation.
themes.name: Acute Clinical Symptoms

themes.disagreements: Renal markers show high consistency in treatment prediction but lower, more variable support for outcome prognosis.
themes.interpretation: Candidates measuring kidney performance demonstrate strong predictive signals for treatment assignment and moderate signals for effect modification.
themes.name: Renal Function

themes.disagreements: Deconditioning shows strong signals across roles, whereas CRP level evidence is weak and lacks consistency.
themes.interpretation: Measures of general patient health, inflammation, and infection status provide evidence for both outcome prognosis and treatment effect heterogeneity.
themes.name: Systemic and Clinical Status

themes.disagreements: Treatment and outcome signals are moderate, while the causal forest provides the strongest supporting signal for the effect modification role.
themes.interpretation: Blood pressure demonstrates a moderate relationship with treatment and outcome, coupled with a strong signal for effect modification.
themes.name: Hemodynamics

themes.disagreements: Cough productivity shows a moderate outcome signal but lacks the treatment or effect signals necessary for a confounder or modifier role.
themes.interpretation: Candidate measurements of cough characteristics and cranial nerve status show minimal or inconsistent evidence across all roles.
themes.name: Cough and Neurological Markers

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
